title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Refrigeration hack hit about 700 French supermarkets; Forescout now counts nearly 13,000 exposed refrigeration control services worldwide
items.content_text: On 22 October Forescout reported 12,976 internet-exposed refrigeration management services on 6,017 IP addresses in 99 countries — the class of web-managed controller that attackers forced into continuous defrost at French supermarkets on the nights of 11–13 October. About 80% of the Danfoss StoreView services it saw ran firmware older than 4.3.1. In France, the finance minister put the toll at about 700 stores, at chains including Carrefour, Coopérative U, E.Leclerc, Intermarché and Monoprix; the Paris prosecutor says the attacks also caused fires, and its cybercrime section is investigating with OFAC and ANSSI. CERT-FR’s alert names Danfoss AK-SC and AK-SM controllers and, since 13 October, Copeland and Dixell XWEB; its latest revision (16 October) says the campaigns are probably still under way. Most affected units are end-of-life, and on 20 October The Record reported that the EU Cyber Resilience Act will not compel fixes for them. No actor, CVE or confirmed entry route has been named, and no new attack nights have been reported since 13 October.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Forescout Vedere Labs (22 Oct 2026); CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 (v1 12 Oct, v2 13 Oct adding Copeland and Dixell XWEB, v3 16 Oct); The Record (20 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek (15 Oct 2026); AP via News4JAX (13 Oct 2026); Danfoss statement (12 Oct 2026)
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Attacks on the nights of 11–13 Oct 2026, none reported since; latest CERT-FR revision 16 Oct 2026 (campaigns probably still ongoing); updated 22 Oct 2026 with Forescout exposure data — investigation ongoing

items.title: The FortiOS flaw behind Unit 42’s Peerstitch case enters CISA KEV, after a FortiManager compromise exposed more than 500 managed firewalls
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2025-61624, a FortiOS command-line path-traversal flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 16 October, two days after Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 described its use. In that case attackers exploited FortiManager (CVE-2024-47575) at a telecommunications managed service provider and took configuration and credential material for more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls; Unit 42 calls this exposure, not confirmed intrusion into those customers’ networks. They then used CVE-2025-61624 to get root on managed FortiGates and drop the Peerstitch loader, and wiped logs and rogue accounts. Unit 42 tracks the cluster as CL-STA-0954 (also UNC5820); it overlaps with suspected nation-state intrusions, but no state is named. Fortinet fixed the flaw in April and rates it Medium because it needs privileged access. The CVE record also lists Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808, which runs FortiOS, as affected.

items.title: CISA, the FBI and partners warn that SafePay ransomware has hit at least 600 organizations since August 2024
items.content_text: Advisory AA26-293A, issued on 20 October by CISA, the FBI and the US Secret Service with Germany’s LKA Rheinland-Pfalz, the UK National Crime Agency and the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit, says SafePay has hit at least 600 organizations from multiple critical-infrastructure sectors in North America, South America, Europe and Australia. Entry is usually through exposed or brute-forced credentials, phished accounts, VPN logins from Mullvad addresses and automated exploitation of edge-device flaws; the group then steals data, deletes shadow copies, resets network-attached storage that holds backups and moves with tools such as WinRM, PsExec and RDP. The advisory carries indicators and ATT&CK mappings for activity from November 2024 to August 2026. It names no victims, and reporting on it describes no OT, energy or water impact, so the OT risk here is the usual one: a ransomware crew reaching the IT network that plant systems depend on.
tags: Advisory — joint advisory AA26-293A from CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service and German and UK partners on SafePay ransomware, which the agencies say has hit at least 600 organizations across multiple critical-infrastructure sectors

items.title: Microsoft assesses China-state-aligned Storm-0940 was behind the ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise, using an AI agent framework to move fast
items.content_text: Microsoft said on 21 October that it assesses Storm-0940, which it calls a China-state-aligned actor, was responsible for the ConnectWise supply-chain compromise. The attackers controlled the identities of ConnectWise cloud applications tied to its Cloud Backup service (formerly SkyKick) and used the apps’ own credentials to try to sign in to more than 2,250 customer Microsoft 365 tenants; a separate password spray on 10–14 October did not succeed. Most targeting failed, but some attacks reached privileged cloud access in under three hours, followed by directory reconnaissance and new app credentials for persistence. Microsoft says ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent penetration-testing framework that can use any AI model, automated reconnaissance, spraying and OAuth abuse. Sectors it lists include energy, chemicals, manufacturing, automotive, aerospace and defense, and government. ConnectWise suspended Cloud Backup and two related services and began a phased restoration on 21 October. No CVE or OT impact is involved; the concern for plant operators is the provider path.

items.title: Albert Heijn restarts home deliveries after the Ahold Delhaize cyberattack; the group confirms malicious activity, and stores stayed open
items.content_text: Albert Heijn restarted grocery home deliveries on 23 October, nearly two weeks after Ahold Delhaize took systems offline on 12 October across most of its brands in Europe and the US (NL Times). In its latest statement, on 19 October, the group said outside experts had confirmed “malicious actions of others”, that it had notified the Dutch NCSC and filed a police report, and that it had no evidence so far that sensitive data was taken; stores stayed open throughout. Stop & Shop and Hannaford sites were back on 20 October, according to the company as quoted by the Boston Globe; no restoration status has been confirmed for Food Lion or Giant. Albert Heijn said its distribution centres had to be restarted on 13–14 October (as reported by NL Times). No attacker or ransomware claim is known. This was an IT-side attack that disrupted logistics, not a confirmed OT compromise, and the Dutch NCSC saw no link to the French refrigeration attack.
tags: Incident — cyberattack on a major grocery group’s IT and online services that disrupted logistics; not a confirmed OT compromise (Food & Ag-adjacent)

items.title: A third Citrix NetScaler zero-day is exploited, and a fourth critical flaw was patched on 9 October
items.content_text: Citrix has confirmed a third NetScaler zero-day under attack, days after patching two others that were exploited for weeks before disclosure, and on 9 October it shipped a fourth fix. The exploited trio is CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88779; the federal KEV deadline for the newest passed on 7 October. The earlier pair brought web shells, rogue admin accounts and stolen configurations, and patching does not evict an intruder. The new CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS v4.0 9.5) is a SAML memory overflow that could allow code execution; no exploitation is reported, but appliances patched last week need another upgrade. Shadowserver counts more than 20,000 internet-exposed NetScaler fingerprints. Because NetScaler often fronts remote access into plant networks, an unhunted appliance is a possible foothold toward OT.
tags: Incident — three NetScaler zero-days confirmed exploited, state-sponsored actors suspected by Mandiant (not attributed); a fourth critical flaw patched 9 Oct, no exploitation reported

items.title: Ivanti warns attackers chained three zero-day flaws, one still unpatched, to take root on fully patched Connect Secure VPNs
items.content_text: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that a small number of customers were hit through a chain of three zero-day flaws that gave unauthenticated, root-level code execution on fully patched Connect Secure appliances. Volexity, which found it while investigating a customer incident, dates its case to 3 October (other researchers saw activity from 1 October) and tracks a previously undocumented actor, UTA0576. The intruders stole domain credentials stored on the appliance, searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, sprayed passwords and scanned internal networks, but left no web shell or backdoor. Volexity judges, with low confidence, that the group is financially motivated, and, with medium confidence, that it uses AI models for exploit development. Fixes cover two of the flaws (CVE-2026-104935); the third, a privilege-escalation bug, is still unpatched. VPN gateways like this commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary.
tags: Incident — Ivanti Connect Secure VPN zero-day chain exploited on fully patched appliances since early Oct; new actor UTA0576 tracked by Volexity; one flaw still unpatched; no OT victim named

items.title: FBI and Secret Service say the FortiBleed campaign against Fortinet VPN gateways is still running
items.content_text: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 6 October that attackers are still scanning internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways with credentials harvested earlier in the campaign. First documented in June, it had collected more than 86,000 working device credentials across 194 countries by 19 June, according to The Hacker News. No vulnerability is involved: the attackers rely on reused or leaked passwords, interception of login traffic and cracking of weakly stored hashes. Some victims were locked out when attackers created new admin accounts, then deleted or reset the legitimate ones; the FBI also says the chain has served as an entry point for ransomware affiliates, and the agencies say targets span all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors, including energy and food and agriculture. Researchers describe a Russian-speaking operator that may be selling access, with overlaps to INC and Lynx ransomware; that attribution is reported, not confirmed. Fortinet gateways often sit at the IT/OT boundary.
tags: Incident — FBI and Secret Service re-warn that the “FortiBleed” credential-harvesting campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains active; reused or leaked credentials, no CVE; no OT victim named

items.title: Booz Allen: frontier AI models went from a perimeter breach to a control-zone action in just over 16 minutes in a lab test
items.content_text: Booz Allen’s 8 October report, From Digital to Physical: The AI Threat Is Here, describes tests in its isolated OT lab in Chantilly, Virginia, modelled on a manufacturing facility. Frontier models from several unnamed vendors met all eight test objectives, going from a perimeter compromise to energising an output on a controller in just over 16 minutes, with a human required to approve every exploit and physical action. One agent found a robotic arm’s API, gained admin access and moved the arm, and a SCADA gateway holding live authenticated sessions to 14 devices gave the models a ready path. Some controls held: one controller rejected a stop command, and local-control mode blocked a remote motor start. Booz Allen calls the results preliminary; some known flaws were left unpatched on purpose and no zero-days were developed. Its Kyle Miller told Dark Reading that removing the approval step would likely have roughly halved the time.
tags: Research — Booz Allen Hamilton lab test of frontier AI models moving from an IT foothold into an industrial control environment

items.title: Accenture, Dragos and SANS launch a $10 million programme to put OT monitoring in up to 500 small utilities
items.content_text: The Community Cyber Resilience Foundation, announced on 20 October by Accenture, Dragos and the SANS Institute with Elastic providing technology support, offers free OT security help to small water, wastewater, electric and natural gas utilities with under $100 million in annual revenue. Dragos describes it as a US programme; the foundation’s own site also mentions Canada. Participants get the Dragos Platform, Neighborhood Keeper and OT-CERT; Accenture assessment, deployment and ongoing support; SANS training with GIAC certification; and hardware funding where needed. About $10 million in funding and services covers a first phase of up to 500 utilities, on top of the 100-plus already in Dragos’s Community Defense Program, and enrollment “opens soon”. It is a resource announcement, not a threat report, but it reaches the small operators that have struggled to fund OT monitoring (editorial assessment).

items.title: Claroty Team82: an AI coding agent rebuilt working exploits for Danfoss refrigeration controllers in about 28 minutes, for roughly $6
items.content_text: Team82 gave an AI coding agent public firmware, the public identifiers of three previously disclosed Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws (CVE-2025-41450, -41451 and -41452) and standard analysis tools, and asked it to recreate working exploits. The agent reproduced two quickly but got the authentication bypass wrong until a researcher redirected it and added a decompiler (Ghidra) integration; it then chained the bypass with command injection to get root on a lab device. Total time was about 28 minutes and about $6 in AI usage. Team82 stresses this was not autonomous discovery: it started from known CVEs and needed human steering. The research appeared as the French supermarket attacks unfolded, but no link to the attackers’ method has been established.
tags: Research — Claroty Team82 lab test of AI-assisted exploit development against Danfoss AK-SM 800A; builds on earlier CVEs

items.title: Siemens confirms a Software Center flaw is being exploited to deliver malware, and CISA adds it to the KEV catalog
items.content_text: Siemens first published CVE-2026-110936 on 15 October and on 19 October confirmed it is being exploited. Software Center, the tool engineers use to install and update Siemens software, did not restrict where it searches for helper DLLs, so attackers paired a genuine, validly signed copy with their own malicious libraries in an installer package. Siemens ties the activity to the “Romulus” multi-platform ClickFix campaign, which tricks users into running pasted commands, and names no final malware family. It says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached, to its knowledge. Version 4.0.9.8 fixes the flaw, and installed copies update on next start. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 20 October with a 3 November deadline and has republished Siemens’ advisory as ICSA-26-295-03. Exploitation needs local access and a user who runs the lure, so engineering workstations running Siemens tooling are the exposure.

items.title: PHP2Shell reaches OT software: Schneider says EcoStruxure Control Engineering has no fix yet, as attempts against the PHP flaws run into the millions
items.content_text: PHP2Shell is a pair of unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS v4.0 9.2) that the PHP project fixed on 21 October in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 after details leaked early. Amazon saw exploitation attempts from 17 October, four days before the patches, and attempts now run into the millions, though no successful compromise has been confirmed. On 22 October Schneider Electric listed three affected products: EcoStruxure Security Expert is fixed in 1.48.4.0 (through Customer Care), owners of ProLeiT LINEoptimize (formerly Plant iT LMS) should get remediation from ProLeiT support, and EcoStruxure Control Engineering has no fix yet while Schneider prepares a remediation plan. ABB has published a notice on PHP2Shell’s impact on APROL, and Moxa a response notice. Industrial software that bundles PHP is easy to miss in IT patch sweeps (editorial assessment), so OT teams should ask their vendors directly.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks patches a PAN-OS zero-day that gives root through the management interface; CISA lists it as exploited
items.content_text: Palo Alto Networks disclosed on 14 October that CVE-2026-0322 lets an attacker who already has credentials and network reach to the PAN-OS management interface run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama appliances. The company reports very limited exploitation and published three attacker IP addresses; Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected. Fixes cover PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2, (the 11.2.16 build was scheduled for 15 October), and there is no workaround beyond limiting management access to trusted internal addresses. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a federal deadline of 17 October. Firewalls like these often sit on the IT/OT boundary, so a management interface reachable from corporate networks or the internet is the exposure to remove. BleepingComputer did not get answers on who is behind the attacks or whether intruders moved further inside.

items.title: October ICS fixes: critical ICONICS GENESIS64 flaws and a WAGO controller bug join Siemens, Rockwell and ABB, and some Siemens flaws still have no fix
items.content_text: On 22 October CISA republished Siemens’ 13 October advisories (ICSA-26-295-02 to -18): fixes are still pending for the S7 PLC web server, the S7-1500 MFP Linux subsystems and WinCC V7.5, and none is planned for APOGEE MBC/MEC. CISA’s 20 October batch covered WAGO controller firmware (CVE-2026-80466, CVSS v3.1 8.8: a low-privileged user can inject commands that run as root; fixed in 4.10.0/FW32) and Moxa’s AIG-302 edge gateway (hard-coded key CVE-2026-109813, v3.1 8.1 / v4.0 8.6; fixed in 1.4.1). Mitsubishi Electric’s 15 October advisory fixes an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-16436, v4.0 9.2) and over-permissive DCOM defaults (CVE-2026-16438, v4.0 9.4) across ICONICS GENESIS64, GENESIS, Hyper Historian and related products; MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz get no fix. Earlier in the month Rockwell fixed a critical 1732E ArmorBlock admin-takeover flaw and ABB a dynovaPRO password-reset flaw. None is reported exploited.

items.title: BeyondTrust patches a Remote Support zero-day exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus espionage actor
items.content_text: BeyondTrust has fixed CVE-2026-102764, an authentication bypass in self-hosted Remote Support appliances (version 26.2.3 and earlier) that lets an unprivileged remote attacker perform file operations. Mandiant and Google’s threat-intelligence group link the exploitation to a suspected state-sponsored espionage actor they track as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221); CrowdStrike calls it Warp Panda. After getting in, the intruders used web shells, escalated to root, wiped logs and harvested stored credentials for lateral movement. SaaS customers were patched on 8 October; self-hosted customers must patch themselves. Shadowserver counts more than 1,400 exposed instances, and Google expects opportunistic exploitation to follow. No victims are named, and none is reported in critical infrastructure. Integrators and OEMs often use this class of tool for vendor access to plants, so its owners should check it. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 16 October with a three-day deadline. We did not find a CVSS score, so none is given.
tags: Advisory — BeyondTrust Remote Support authentication-bypass zero-day (BT26-05), exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor; vendor remote-access tooling often used to reach plant systems; no OT victims named

items.title: Two threat-intel firms report exploitation attempts against SonicWall’s maximum-severity SMA1000 flaw, days after hotfixes shipped
items.content_text: Previdian and Defused both report their honeypots receiving requests consistent with CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS 10), a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the SMA1000 WorkPlace interface that SonicWall patched on 6 October; Defused dates its first hits to 8 October (SecurityWeek, 12 October). Neither has determined whether any attempt succeeded, and SonicWall’s advisory did not flag active exploitation. Fixed builds are 12.5.0-03082 and 12.4.3-03670. The flaw is reachable remotely without authentication on SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v models; SMA100 and firewall SSL-VPN are not affected. Shadowserver counts more than 400 exposed SMA1000 appliances. The same interface was hit by SSRF flaws in July and September that were exploited, so quick scanning after a patch is plausible. These gateways often give vendors and integrators a path toward plant networks.
tags: Advisory — SonicWall rates CVE-2026-102255, an SSRF in the SMA1000 Appliance WorkPlace interface, as maximum severity; unauthenticated and remote; two threat-intel firms report exploitation attempts (not confirmed successful); not in CISA KEV as of CISA’s 21 Oct catalog

items.title: FERC staff publish CIP audit lessons: unregistered new generation, stacked low-impact systems and AI tools in CIP networks
items.content_text: On 13 October FERC released a staff report drawing on its fiscal-2026 audits of NERC-registered entities. Most cybersecurity processes reviewed met the mandatory CIP standards, but auditors found three recurring problems. Some generator owners registered new resources late or never identified their BES Cyber Systems, and several inverter-based resources were running commercially without the required cyber evaluation, one more than a year past the threshold. Two entities treated systems as low impact that together met the medium-impact criteria once affiliate and contractor control was counted. Auditors also saw what the report calls “super intelligence” (SI) tools — chatbots, assistants and automated analytics — appearing inside CIP-networked environments, where they can mimic user behavior and open unauthorized access or lateral-movement paths faster than compliance programs adapt. The report is staff guidance, not a new requirement, and it suggests NERC may consider further guidance or standards changes.
